text.name: revamp_descBuy
text.text: Buy goods from the retailer and have them delivered. Note: The retailer charges more if they deliver themselves.

text.name: revamp_descSell
text.text: Sell goods to a dealer. Note: The dealer pays less if they have to pick up the goods themselves.

text.name: revamp_manageSharedStorageHint
text.text: These goods share a storage capacity of %s.

text.name: revamp_descDistributionLimit
text.text: Up to which stock level should this target be supplied?

text.name: revamp_animalDeliveryDescription
text.text: How much an animal is worth depends on its type, its age and its health.

text.name: revamp_animalAgeError
text.text: Animals need to be between %s and %s months old.

text.name: revamp_animalAgeErrorFrom
text.text: Animals need to be at least %s months old.

text.name: revamp_animalHealthError
text.text: Animals need a health between %s %% and %s %%.

text.name: revamp_animalNotValid
text.text: This animal type is not accepted here.

text.name: revamp_animalNotValidForTrigger
text.text: This animal type is not accepted at this trigger.

text.name: revamp_animalNoSpace
text.text: The storage of this production is full.

text.name: revamp_setting_distributionActive_tooltip
text.text: Turns distribution between production points on or off. When off the game distributes on its own again, the configured targets are kept.

text.name: revamp_setting_distributionCostFactor_tooltip
text.text: Defines how expensive distributing goods between production points is. At 0 % delivery is free, at 200 % every delivery costs twice as much.

text.name: revamp_setting_storageActive_tooltip
text.text: Turns the “Store” output mode and the manual unloading as pallets or bales on or off. When off, stored goods behave like “Keep”, the setting itself is kept.

text.name: revamp_setting_buyingActive_tooltip
text.text: Allows buying ingredients directly at the production point.

text.name: revamp_setting_sellingActive_tooltip
text.text: Allows selling products directly at the production point.

text.name: revamp_setting_tradeRestriction_tooltip
text.text: Defines who may buy ingredients and sell products at a production point. “Production manager” means anyone holding the “Manage productions” permission.

text.name: revamp_setting_directSellingPriceFactor_tooltip
text.text: Defines how much selling directly at the production point pays. 100 % equals the full market price.

text.name: revamp_setting_weatherModesActive_tooltip
text.text: Defines whether recipes may depend on weather, season and time of day. When off, every production line runs at full rate around the clock.

text.name: revamp_setting_recipeSettingsActive_tooltip
text.text: Defines whether players may choose which ingredient and booster a production line uses. When off, the production's own setting always applies.

text.name: revamp_setting_showSharedIcon_tooltip
text.text: Shows in the production menu whether a production point runs all its lines at once or one after another.

text.name: revamp_setting_showBuildingCosts_tooltip
text.text: Shows the monthly upkeep of every production point in the production menu.

text.name: revamp_setting_showDistributionTargets_tooltip
text.text: Shows behind every product in the output list where it is delivered to first.

text.name: revamp_help_menu_dualRole
text.text: A good that is both an ingredient and a product at the same production point used to be listed twice. It now appears once, in its own section between the incoming materials and the outgoing products.

text.name: revamp_help_menu_shared
text.text: An asterisk behind an amount means several goods share the same storage space. The capacity shown is what is currently still free for that good, and it drops as soon as one of the others grows. The size of the shared space is shown in the info box below.

text.name: revamp_help_menu_extras
text.text: Below the name of each production point you can see its monthly building costs. The symbol next to a production line shows whether the point runs all lines at the same time or one after another. Both can be hidden in the settings.

text.name: revamp_help_menu_buttons
text.text: The bar at the bottom gains “Manage” and “Take out goods”. Both are also available directly at the building, without going through the menu.

text.name: revamp_help_recipe_intro
text.text: The recipe of a production line is shown on the right of the production menu. Above the ingredients you see the conditions under which the line runs at all, below them the ingredients themselves, and last what comes out of it.

text.name: revamp_help_recipe_mix
text.text: Ingredients under a shared heading are alternatives: only one of them is needed, and the line keeps running as long as one of them is in storage. That is how a recipe asks for “any kind of grain” instead of wheat specifically. Which one is used is set in the manage dialog under “Production lines”.

text.name: revamp_help_recipe_boost
text.text: Boosters are optional extra ingredients that increase the yield. If they run out, production carries on and simply pays less. The booster group shows which factor is currently in effect, and the recipe shows the combined effect of all boosters together.

text.name: revamp_help_recipe_master
text.text: A master booster speeds up the whole line instead of only increasing the yield: more is consumed and more is produced. Of several master boosters only ever one is in effect, and which one that is you set in the manage dialog just like the ingredient choice.

text.name: revamp_help_weather_intro
text.text: Some production lines depend on the weather or on the time of day. A bakery has opening hours, a solar dryer only works in sunshine, a windmill depends on the wind. What applies to a line is shown in the recipe above the ingredients, one line per condition.

text.name: revamp_help_weather_stop
text.text: When a line is standing still, the production menu names the reason instead of “running”: outside opening hours, wrong season, wrong month, or not enough weather. A line stopped like this consumes nothing, produces nothing and costs no running expenses either. That is different from a line missing an ingredient – that one keeps running and is only waiting for material.

text.name: revamp_help_weather_speed
text.text: With the weather a line does not stop but works at different speeds. How strongly the weather is affecting it right now is shown in the info box next to status, cycles and costs. Some lines have a base load and keep running slowly even in the worst weather.

text.name: revamp_help_weather_storage
text.text: A storage can also fill or empty through the weather with no production at all, a rain barrel for example. That works even when no production is switched on at the point.

text.name: revamp_help_manage_intro
text.text: The manage dialog lists all goods of a production point with exact amounts instead of bars only, split by whether they are an ingredient, a product, or both.

text.name: revamp_help_manage_output
text.text: For every product you decide what should happen to it: keep it in storage, sell it right away, distribute it to other production points, or store it and take it out later as pallets or bales.

text.name: revamp_help_manage_trade
text.text: Ingredients can be bought and products sold right at the production point, without driving anything. Buying costs more and selling pays less than at the market, so the convenience has a price. Individual goods can be excluded from this.

text.name: revamp_help_manage_views
text.text: The confirm key switches between goods, production lines and distribution, plus animals at a production that accepts them. In the production lines you choose which ingredient is used when several are possible. Under distribution you decide which production points receive your products, and in which order.

text.name: revamp_help_distribution_intro
text.text: When a product is set to distribute, the production point sends it once per game hour to your own productions that need it as an ingredient. Who gets how much of it is set in the manage dialog in the “Distribution” view.

text.name: revamp_help_distribution_levels
text.text: The space bar steps the level of each consumer. “Primary” is served first, “Secondary” gets what the primary targets can no longer take, “Remainder” what is left after that, and “Never” nothing at all. Several targets on the same level get equal shares. Without any change every target sits on “Remainder”, which spreads everything evenly.

text.name: revamp_help_distribution_running
text.text: Only whoever is actually processing the good right now is supplied. A production line that is switched off gets nothing, and neither does one standing still because of its opening hours or the weather. The list still shows every possible consumer, including the ones currently switched off.

text.name: revamp_help_distribution_limit
text.text: The limit sets the stock level up to which a target is supplied. “None” stops deliveries entirely, “Full” supplies without a limit. That leaves room for whatever you deliver yourself.

text.name: revamp_help_distribution_costs
text.text: Every delivery costs money depending on amount and distance, and it is charged to the receiver. The list shows per target what that amounts to per hour; a dash means this target gets nothing with the current setting. In the finances overview these costs appear as their own entry, “Delivery costs”.

text.name: revamp_help_spawn_intro
text.text: Stored products can be taken out as pallets, bales or wood logs whenever you want, instead of waiting for the game to place something on its own.

text.name: revamp_help_spawn_how
text.text: Pick the good, then the packaging, then the amount. Bales come as round or square bales in the sizes available for that good, and for wood logs you choose the length. The amount of liters per unit is always shown.

text.name: revamp_help_spawn_options
text.text: Bales that come out wrapped get a wrapping colour of your choice. In multiplayer you also decide which farm the goods should belong to.

text.name: revamp_help_spawn_silo
text.text: A silo built for it can do the same. There it is triggered at its own trigger at the building.

text.name: revamp_help_animals_intro
text.text: Some productions accept live animals as an ingredient, a slaughterhouse for example. They have their own trigger at the building where you pull up with a livestock trailer.

text.name: revamp_help_animals_how
text.text: Drive the trailer to the trigger and stay in the vehicle. Then pick the group of animals from your trailer and how many of them you want to deliver. If a group is not accepted, the reason is shown where the number would be.

text.name: revamp_help_animals_amount
text.text: The amount depends on the animal type, its age and its health: older and healthier animals are worth more. Which animals a production accepts and what they are worth is listed in the manage dialog under “Animals”.

text.name: revamp_help_settings_global
text.text: In the settings, under Game, you find the “Production Revamp” section. There an administrator turns individual features off for everyone and sets who may buy and sell, what distribution costs, and what selling on site pays. Whatever is turned off also disappears from the controls.

text.name: revamp_help_settings_display
text.text: Under General there is also “Production Revamp: Display”. These switches only affect your own screen, change nothing about the game itself, and need no admin rights.

text.name: revamp_help_settings_keep
text.text: Nothing is lost when a feature is turned off: distribution targets, stored goods and the chosen modes stay saved and apply again as soon as the switch is turned back on.
